channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan Launch Trans-Caspian Digital Cable, Bypassing Russia
item.description: A new 380-kilometer fiber-optic cable connects Aktau, Kazakhstan, to Sumgayit, Azerbaijan, aiming to reduce Russia's digital connectivity dominance. The Trans-Caspian Fiber Optic Cable (TCFOC) has a capacity of 400 terabits per second and is part of a regional push for digital sovereignty. Kazakhstan anticipates significant transit traffic, potentially reaching 21.6 Tbps.

item.title: US Deputy Secretary of State Discusses Trans-Caspian Trade with Turkmenistan Leaders
item.description: US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met with Turkmen leaders in Ashgabat to discuss expanding trans-Caspian trade and transport routes. Discussions included potential cooperation on regional infrastructure initiatives and the development of trans-Caspian transport links. The Turkmen government noted "fruitful" bilateral contacts yielding positive results.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Mandatory Housing Insurance Against Natural Disasters
item.description: Kazakhstan is developing a mandatory housing insurance system to cover damages from earthquakes, floods, and wildfires. Property owners would pay annual contributions to a special fund, intended to provide faster aid to victims and reduce the state budget burden. Experts have mixed opinions, with some supporting the reform and others concerned about new fees.

item.title: Military Helicopter Crashes in Central Turkey, Killing Five Personnel
item.description: Five military personnel died when a military helicopter crashed in the central Turkish city of Eskişehir during a training flight. The AS-532 type helicopter belonged to the Air Force Command. The Ministry of National Defense confirmed the crash, and search and rescue operations are ongoing at the wreckage site.

item.title: Taliban Authorities Force Afghan Men to Restrict Female Family Members
item.description: Afghan men and women have reported that Taliban authorities are compelling men to impose strict restrictions on female family members. These restrictions reportedly include forbidding women from leaving their homes and withholding their cell phones. The Taliban's actions aim to enforce their interpretation of social and personal freedoms for women.

item.title: RFE/RL Resumes Shortwave Broadcasts in Afghanistan with Educational Programs for Girls
item.description: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL) has returned to shortwave radio broadcasting in Afghanistan, offering new educational programming for girls excluded from school by the Taliban. The broadcasts, which began November 24, include three hours of educational content, news, analysis, and music, targeting girls aged 12-17.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes State Visit to Jordan, Strategic Partnership Established
item.description: The state visit of the President of Uzbekistan to the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan has concluded. During the visit, President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held productive talks with King Abdullah II in Amman and participated in a business forum. An agreement establishing a strategic partnership and 19 other cooperation documents were signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Jordan to Expand Business Cooperation
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the opening of the Uzbek-Jordanian Business Forum. The forum highlighted the growth in bilateral relations, with trade volume increasing nearly ninefold in five years. An agreement on preferential trade was signed, aiming to boost mutual product supplies.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses Progress and Challenges in Digitalizing Healthcare
item.description: Uzbekistan's Minister of Health presented on the digitalization of the healthcare system, highlighting progress in equipping medical facilities with computers and implementing the DMED information system. The ministry aims to increase computer coverage to 94% by year-end and has saved significant funds through IT maintenance. Challenges and solutions were also discussed.

item.title: Most Vulnerable Passwords Revealed; Experts Advise on Cybersecurity Measures
item.description: A study by NordPass identified the most common and easily cracked passwords globally, with '123456' topping the list. Experts warn that even complex-looking passwords can be quickly compromised. They recommend using passkeys, strong unique passwords of at least 15 characters, password managers, and two-factor authentication to enhance online security and protect personal data.

item.title: NGOs in Helmand Report Taliban Interference and Obstacles to Operations
item.description: Local sources in Helmand report that the Taliban's interference in the affairs of organizations, creating obstacles and delaying their activities, has made some institutions reluctant to continue operating. A committee reportedly oversees NGO activities, demanding privileges and delaying operations, affecting everything from recruitment to service delivery.

item.title: Illegal Casino Shut Down in Aktobe, Organizer Arrested
item.description: An illegal gambling operation in Aktobe has been shut down by the Department of Economic Investigations, coordinated by the Mangystau regional prosecutor's office. The operation, which ran from April to October 2026, involved accepting cash bets through gaming terminals. The organizer has been detained.

item.title: Shots Fired Near Atakent in Almaty, Suspect Detained
item.description: Almaty police responded to reports of shots fired near the Atakent exhibition center. A witness reported a man on a bicycle firing a rifle before fleeing. Police apprehended a suspect in a nearby apartment, finding a disassembled shotgun, ammunition, and shell casings. An investigation into illegal arms possession is underway.

item.title: Turkmenistan Strengthens Position as Key Transport and Logistics Hub
item.description: An international conference and exhibition, "International Transport and Transit Corridors: Cooperation and Development - 2026," and the "Turkmentel - 2026" exhibition have commenced in Ashgabat. Over 600 delegates from more than 300 international organizations and companies are participating. Turkmenistan emphasizes cooperation with leading producers and UN bodies to develop key sectors and infrastructure projects.

item.title: UK Employers to Recruit Seasonal Workers from Uzbekistan
item.description: Uzbekistan expects a new recruitment drive for seasonal work in the UK. The Migration Agency reported that over 14,000 Uzbek citizens have worked in the UK since 2023. British operators plan to visit Uzbekistan to select candidates for the upcoming season. Discussions also covered worker rights and legal protections.

item.title: Briefing on International Law Year and UN-CIS Partnership
item.description: A briefing was held at the Turkmen Foreign Ministry focusing on implementing Turkmenistan's international initiatives. Discussions covered the UN General Assembly's resolution declaring 2028 the "International Year of Law" and the national "International Law and Turkmenistan's Neutrality" concept. A draft national action plan for preparing and celebrating this year was presented.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Jordan Sign Preferential Trade Agreement
item.description: Uzbekistan and Jordan signed a preferential trade agreement during a business forum in Amman, aiming to increase mutual product supplies and reach $500 million in trade. The agreement provides for reduced customs duties on 300 types of goods. Both sides expressed confidence in strengthening economic ties and expanding market access.

item.title: 45 Students Expelled from College in Kazakhstan's Kostanay Region
item.description: Forty-five students have been expelled from the Kazakh Agro-Technical College in Karabalyk village, Kostanay region, after a prosecutor's investigation revealed they were registered as students despite not attending classes. The college director was dismissed, and seven instructors faced disciplinary action.

item.title: UN Women Chief Warns Ignoring Violence Against Women Has Deadly Consequences
item.description: UN Women Executive Director Sima Bahous urged immediate support for women facing violence, warning that ignoring abuse signs can lead to fatal outcomes. She stressed the need for safe reporting channels, access to support, and perpetrator accountability, noting that the rate of female homicides is declining slower than the global average.

item.title: Three Arrested in Tashkent for Illegal Crypto Operations Worth $64 Million
item.description: Tashkent's Interior Ministry reported the dismantling of a major scheme involving illegal income laundering through crypto assets. Three individuals were detained for conducting currency exchanges and financial operations, reportedly taking money from businessmen in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. Over $64 million in USDT was found on their devices.

item.title: 45 Students Expelled from Agricultural College in Kazakhstan Over Irregularities
item.description: Forty-five students were expelled from the Kazakh Agro-Technical College in Kostanay region after a prosecutor's check revealed they were enrolled but not attending classes, leading to unjustified budget expenditures. The college director was dismissed, and seven teachers faced disciplinary action.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Jordan plan textile production and boost trade ties.
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Jordanian officials and business leaders to expand economic cooperation. The countries aim to establish joint textile production in Jordan using Uzbek materials and increase trade turnover to $500 million. Investment in mining and pharmaceuticals was also discussed.

item.title: 14 heads of medical institutions in Kyrgyzstan reprimanded for quality of education.
item.description: Fourteen heads of state medical educational institutions in Kyrgyzstan have been reprimanded for failing to ensure the quality of the educational process. The decision was made at a collegium meeting of the Ministry of Health. Disciplinary action was also recommended for rectors of four state universities.

item.title: Fatal Car Crash on Tashkent-Almalyk Highway Claims Three Lives
item.description: A fatal car accident occurred on the Tashkent-Almalyk highway in the Akhangaran district of Tashkent region, resulting in the deaths of three individuals. The driver of a Cobalt lost control and collided with a tree. The 33-year-old driver and his two 32-year-old passengers were pronounced dead at the scene. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Former Son-in-Law of Karim Masimov Requests Case Transfer to National Security Committee
item.description: Azamat Kapenov, former top manager of 'KazTemirTrans' and ex-son-in-law of Karim Masimov, has requested his case be transferred from the Financial Monitoring Agency (FMA) to the National Security Committee (KNB). Kapenov claims he caused no damage and seeks a state audit, alleging his case is politically motivated and involves 'raiding'.

item.title: Doctor and Son Die in Aktobe Region Road Accident
item.description: A tragic incident occurred in the Aktobe region where an ENT doctor, Nazgul Kantorenova, died in a road accident on November 23. Her 21-year-old son, Rasul Bakhtybay, was later reported to have also passed away. Preliminary information suggests his case is being registered as a suicide.

item.title: Houthis Attack Riyadh Financial Center, 11 Injured Reported
item.description: The Houthis carried out an attack on a financial center in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia's capital. According to Saudi civil defense, 11 people were injured in the assault, including two Saudis and nine foreigners. Authorities called the attack terrorism.

item.title: Tashkent Police Arrest Crypto Business Operators with Over $64 Million Turnover
item.description: Tashkent police have uncovered a large-scale illegal currency exchange scheme involving crypto assets. Three individuals were detained on suspicion of concealing the sources of illegally obtained income. Devices seized revealed transactions exceeding $64 million USDT.

item.title: Nighttime Power Outages Possible in 17 Tashkent Neighborhoods
item.description: Residents in Almazar and Shaykhantakhur districts of Tashkent may experience temporary power interruptions on the night of November 25. Specialists will be checking equipment at the "Vystavochnaya" substation between 00:00 and 06:00. The Tashkent Regional Electric Networks apologized for any inconvenience.

item.title: UN Women: Home Should Not Be the Most Dangerous Place for Women
item.description: UN Women has launched its '16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence' campaign, emphasizing that home should not be the most dangerous place for women. The organization calls for a different path to end violence against women, highlighting that femicide is often the final stage of a preventable cycle of violence.

item.title: Switzerland to Return $252 Million in Gulnora Karimova's Assets to Uzbekistan
item.description: Switzerland will return another $252 million from Gulnora Karimova's assets to Uzbekistan. The funds will be directed through the "Ishonch" foundation towards building new schools, improving medical care for children and adolescents, and other social programs.

item.title: Russian Attack in Ukraine Kills Two, Injures 40 in Zaporizhzhia
item.description: A Russian attack on Zaporizhzhia killed two people and injured 40, including four children. Residential buildings and infrastructure were damaged. Russia's Defense Ministry reported strikes on military targets in the Sumy region, claiming to hit drone control centers and satellite terminals.

item.title: Israel Claims Elimination of Hamas Internal Security Commander
item.description: Israel announced the killing of a commander responsible for Hamas's internal security. Further details regarding the operation or the identity of the individual were not immediately provided in the initial report.

item.title: Kazakhstan Disputes Claims of Contributing to Tashkent's Air Pollution
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kazhydromet agency has refuted claims that dust masses from its territory contributed to air pollution in Tashkent. Their research indicates that air currents in late November originated from Iran, the Kyzylkum Desert, and southwestern Uzbekistan, not Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Adjust Maternity Leave Payments Calculation in 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Labor and Social Protection announced changes to maternity leave payment calculations effective in 2027. The adjustments will consider average monthly income over the last 12 months and the duration of leave. Specific coefficients apply for regular, complicated, or multiple births.

item.title: Uzbek President Concludes State Visit to Jordan
item.description: The President of Uzbekistan has concluded a two-day state visit to Jordan. King Abdullah II personally bid farewell to the Uzbek leader and his wife at the airport. During the visit, leaders held negotiations, solidified strategic partnership, exchanged state awards, and attended a business forum.

item.title: WHO Warns of 39 Million Deaths from Antibiotic Resistance by 2050
item.description: The World Health Organization predicts nearly 39 million deaths globally due to antibiotic resistance over the next 25 years. Scientists warn that modern medicine's existence is threatened without effective antibiotics. This invisible threat extends beyond hospitals, impacting various aspects of healthcare.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's State Secretary Inspects Historical Museum's Exhibit Storage
item.description: State Secretary Arslan Koychiev visited the National Historical Museum of Kyrgyzstan to discuss its operations and future development. He reviewed the current condition and storage of museum exhibits. Discussions focused on improving the museum's concept and reflecting historical-cultural heritage according to modern standards.

item.title: European Nations Desire Four-Party Talks in Abu Dhabi, Russia Unconvinced
item.description: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that European countries are seeking four-party talks in Abu Dhabi. However, Russia currently sees no "added value" in participating in the peace settlement process. Peskov indicated differing views on the negotiations and confirmed that no date has been set for the talks.

item.title: Kazakhstan Modifies Additional Payment Procedures for Coaches
item.description: Kazakhstan has updated regulations for additional payments to coaches, effective November 18, 2026. The changes affect civil servants and other employees of state sports organizations funded by the state budget. The amount of additional payments will be determined within the approved payroll fund. Specific rules apply for multiple high achievements in various sports disciplines.
